findings.title: Self-ranking made public
findings.claim: The cheek, imagined likeness, gait, and boast stage an inward claim to rank before other people: 8:47 supplies showy departure and public display, while 3:188 exposes praise claimed for deeds not done.
findings.mechanism: The cheek and voluntary walk are concrete carriers; the imagined likeness supplies a projected self and the boast supplies its merit ledger. The focus people's phrase and the independent scenes of showmanship and praise-seeking make bodily bearing into a social performance rather than a private estimate alone.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can see why the cheek, walk, self-image, and boast work as one public act: rank is not only felt but staged for an audience.
findings.containment: The prohibitions still concern cheek-turning and exultant walking. The wider parallels illuminate their public-status pressure without making every boast identical or claiming that the focus text names a particular contest.

epistemic.reason: Trusted cross-run evidence and direct supplied connection texts ground the relation; a parallel legacy walk is retained as corroboration, while connection-target morphology is not supplied.

The wider contexts distinguish ordinary joy from unjustified exultation, received gifts from self-made rank, and one boastful type from every bearer of that type; their contact makes the prohibition about joy converted into public superiority.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep the joy/boast distinction intact while seeing why the closing divine-love clause is attached to the whole character type.
findings.containment: This does not condemn gratitude or happiness. The wider links specify an ethically charged, comparative performance and do not settle every use of joy elsewhere.

epistemic.reason: Trusted publication evidence and exact connection targets directly repeat the relevant joy/boast relations; legacy reader support confirms overlapping focus branches without controlling the reading.

After, 31:7's sequence of turning away, arrogance, simulated non-hearing, and weighted ears supplies a sensory-refusal circuit that returns through the focus cheek and people. Each HFT role below remains tied to its supplied coordinate; the focus cheek and human target are the return path.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive refusal as an embodied closing of channels, not merely an impolite angle.

A live alternative is that 31:7 concerns rejection of revelation only and does not generalize to interpersonal perception; the focus still plainly prohibits the cheek-turn.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is internally complete and its exact Arabic anchors are supplied, but target morphology is not; the revelation-only alternative is preserved and all unresolved branch glosses remain null.

findings.title: Counterfeit growth on a stable, accountable earth
findings.claim: The focus earth and exultant manner can jar against the stable, fecund earth of 31:10 and the tiny retrievable seed of 31:16: conspicuous pride performs counterfeit growth while overlooking received ground and the moral weight of a minute gesture.
findings.mechanism: Before, earth is only the location of an ostentatious walk. After, 31:10's fixed earth, prevented sway, and emerging growth and 31:16's seed, tiny weight, and subtle concealment turn that ground into a field of received flourishing and fine accountability. The focus manner can then be read as renewed sway and self-inflation. HFT roles are preserved in the branch activations, including growth, strutting, seed, weight, and concealment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the proud walk as a false claim to self-generated growth beside an earth whose life and stability are received and whose smallest act remains known.
findings.containment: This is explicitly exploratory. The live alternative is that 31:10 and 31:16 establish creation and knowledge without commenting specifically on pride; no claim is made that the focus manner literally means agricultural growth.

epistemic.reason: The HFT support itself marks the reading exploratory and states the creation/knowledge alternative; exact Arabic is supplied for 31:10 and 31:16, but contextual segmentation and branch roles remain attributed.

findings.title: Walking as one bounded, supported course

After, 31:29 gives celestial movement an appointed limit, 31:31 attributes a ship's running to grace, and 31:32 moves from engulfing waves to land and moderation. These supplied roles rescale the focus walking verb and earth phrase; qasd's person-level description remains an analogy rather than a gait modifier.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the difference between moving through a course and owning the conditions that let movement continue.

epistemic.reason: HFT marks the course model medium-confidence and names qasd/person-versus-gait as an alternative; exact Arabic anchors are supplied but contextual morphology and roles remain attributed.

findings.title: A polished self as false proxy and forecast
findings.claim: Arrogance can install a polished image and merit-story as substitutes for the accountable self and as guarantees of a route whose next gain and endpoint remain unknown; 57:23 and 3:188 show how received gifts or unperformed deeds can be miscounted as personal distinction.
findings.mechanism: Before, arrogance is an excessive estimate of present worth. After, 31:33's non-substitution and worldly-deception warning and 31:34's unknown next gain and place of death turn the focus likeness and boast into a false proxy and forecast. The HFT roles below preserve the face, attractive deception, withheld knowledge, and road-direction echo; the last remains form-distant.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how status display depends on both a self-image that stands in for accountability and a future that the image cannot secure.
findings.containment: The alternative remains live that 31:33–34 concern eschatological deception and unknown destiny without targeting ordinary self-presentation. The focus words retain their ordinary senses; no future-specific meaning is assigned to boast.

epistemic.reason: The HFT course has exact Arabic anchors but attributed contextual segmentation and roles; connected 57:23/3:188 texts ground gift/merit misaccounting while the eschatological-only reading remains possible.
